rules.statement: A decree nisi for dissolution of a marriage does not terminate the status of the parties as husband and wife until the decree absolute is made. The date of the decree absolute, rather than the decree nisi, determines when the marriage is legally dissolved.
rules.supporting_quote: "It is clear law that the entry of decree nisi for dissolution of a marriage does not terminate the status of the parties as husband and wife. In the Aserappa case [ 1 (1935) 37 N. L. R. 372. ] , this Court disapproved of a practice sometimes adopted of a Court entering a decree absolute without being moved to do so by one of the parties ; and in the de Silva case [ 2 (1936) 38 N. L. R. 63. ] the Privy Council referred to the need for an application to be made by a party before the Court makes absolute the decree of dissolution."
